draft.title: Pronouns and connectives for cohesion
card: Cohesion is how a text holds together, so that one sentence leads smoothly to the next. Pronouns and connectives are two tools that build it.
a word such as he, she, it or they that stands in for a noun. It must point clearly to one noun. In "Mia told Zoe she was late", we cannot tell who was late.
a word or phrase that links ideas across sentences. However shows contrast, therefore shows a result, and meanwhile shows that two things happen at the same time.
A connective must match the link between the ideas. Using the wrong one, such as therefore for a contrast, confuses the reader.
draft.remember: Clear pronouns and well-chosen connectives help a reader follow your ideas.

a.q: Which sentence has a pronoun that could point to more than one noun?
opts: Sam told Leo he had won the race
Sam told Leo that Sam had won the race
Sam smiled because he had won the race
Sam ran fast, so he won the race
a.why: In the first sentence, he could mean Sam or Leo, so the reader cannot be sure. In the last two, he can only mean Sam, because only one person is named before it.
a.clue: Look for a pronoun with two possible people it could mean.

b.q: Ava's first sentence says the bushwalk was long and tiring. Her second says the group enjoyed the view from the top. Which connective, placed at the start of the second sentence, links them best?
opts: However
Therefore
Meanwhile
For example
b.why: The second sentence is a contrast with the first: the walk was tiring, but the view was enjoyed. However shows contrast. Therefore is tempting, but it shows a result, and enjoying the view is not a result of being tired.
b.clue: Does the second sentence add to the first, or push against it?

a.best: Sam told Leo he had won the race

problems.detail: The why refers to options by position ('the first sentence', 'the last two'), but options are shown in random order. It also skips one of the three wrong options. It says 'he' can only mean Sam because only one person is named before it, which is false for 'Sam told Leo that Sam had won the race': that sentence names two people and has no pronoun 'he' at all. The why should name each sentence and explain the repeated-name option correctly.
